items.title: QC10 Clean And Dirty Ancillas

items.statement_or_definition: Input an explicit topologically ordered bounded-fan-in Boolean DAG over NOT, AND, OR with n inputs, m output ports and constants. Allocate zero work for each gate value and distinct clean scratch for repeated input ports. Evaluate nodes in order: constants use I/X; NOT uses X(t) then CNOT(a,t); AND uses Toffoli(a,b,t); OR uses CNOT(a,t),CNOT(b,t),Toffoli(a,b,t). Copy repeated source ports into distinct scratch by CNOT, use them, and uncopy. CNOT each designated output value into the corresponding arbitrary target y bit. Reverse every compute instruction to restore work. Output the explicit finite gate list implementing |x,y,0_work> to |x,y xor f(x),0_work>. Domain requires a finite DAG; invalid wire references/cycles/unknown labels return INVALID rather than a gate list.
proof_obligations: The algorithm gives finite topological loops and inverse-list output; mathematical correctness, clean-work restoration and costs belong to the following results.

items.title: Exact Arbitrary Unitary QSD Upper Bound

items.statement_or_definition: For a circuit skeleton on n qubits with m CNOTs and arbitrary one-qubit gates, prove that its parameterized image has real dimension at most \(3n+4m+1\): the initial local layer contributes at most \(3n\), each CNOT contributes at most four new parameters by the local stabilizer/coset calculation, and one scalar accounts for global phase. There are finitely many skeletons for fixed n,m, so if \(3n+4m+1<4^n=\dim U(2^n)\), their smooth images have measure zero. This yields the generic lower bound in the following theorem.
proof_obligations: Parameterize one-qubit gates by SU(2) Euler charts plus one aggregate scalar. Immediately before each CNOT, a Z rotation on the control and an X rotation on the target commute through that CNOT and can be absorbed into the preceding local layer. These are two independent one-dimensional stabilizer directions out of the six local parameters on that pair, leaving at most four new parameters.

Iterate this absorption to obtain finitely/countably many smooth parameter charts of dimension ≤3n+4m+1. items.statement_or_definition: Show the projective Clifford+T one-qubit subgroup is dense: normalize \(H,T\) into \(h=iH\in SU(2)\) and \(t=e^{-i\pi/8}T\in SU(2)\), take \(V=ht\), and compute \(\operatorname{tr}V=\sqrt2\sin(\pi/8)=x\). Powers of V are dense on one SU(2) torus; conjugation by t gives a nonparallel axis; an explicit two-axis Euler/coordinate lemma yields all SU(2). The normalized matrices are SU(2) lifts of raw H/T labels; translating the resulting word back to raw labels preserves only the projective class unless its scalar is tracked.

items.statement_or_definition: For fixed k, factor an exact target \(U\in U(2^k)\) by QC11 into \(m(k)\) one-qubit \(U(2)\) gates and \(c(k)\) exact CNOTs. Write each one-qubit gate as \(e^{i\phi_j}S_j\), with \(S_j\in SU(2)\), and compile only the \(S_j\) factors by SK. For the resulting fixed-width circuit C, the guaranteed metric is \(\min_{|\lambda|=1}\|U-\lambda C\|_{op}\le\varepsilon\), with at most \(m(k)\) compiler calls at accuracy \(\varepsilon/m(k)\); telescoping gives this whole-circuit projective bound. Its gate count is at most \(c(k)+O(m(k)\log^{\log_{3/2}5}(m(k)/\varepsilon))\), with no ancillas. Consequently every input-state/output-event probability changes by at most \(2\varepsilon\). This is a channel-level guarantee for the entire unconditional block, not operator-norm approximation to a prescribed representative. A strict representative-level bound requires an explicit phase-carrying primitive/decomposition.
proof_obligations: QC11 exact factorization, one-qubit SU(2) compiler, root norm inequalities. The CSD angle algorithm's finite input representation and branch handling remain explicit.

items.statement_or_definition: Fix a finite gate alphabet of maximum arity k≤3, n classical input wires, zero-initialized ancillas and one designated measured output bit (no arbitrary classical acceptance predicate for free). Restrict to C≥n gates and at most n+kC+1 active wires after removing unused ancillas. There are at most sum_(j≤C)(A(n+kC+1)^k)^j output-designated descriptions, i.e. exp(O(C log C)). Each circuit can compute at most one Boolean function with success≥2/3 on every input. Counting against 2^(2^n) shows that for all sufficiently large n at least 99% of Boolean functions require Omega(2^n/n) gates. If arbitrary classical postprocessing is allowed, include its circuit/description cost; otherwise this conclusion is false.
proof_obligations: Count every gate label, ordered wire tuple and chosen output wire. For C of order 2^n/n the logarithm of the description count is at most a chosen fixed fraction of 2^n; choose a sufficiently small constant.

For a fixed circuit, output-one probability cannot be ≥2/3 and ≤1/3 on the same input; hence each truth table has at most one interpretation. Divide the number of descriptions by 2^(2^n), absorbing polynomial factors.

items.statement_or_definition: For Pauli errors E and ordered Hermitian generators g_j, syndrome bit j is 0 for Eg_j=g_jE and 1 for Eg_j=−g_jE. Let Z(P_n)={i^k I}. Logical Pauli classes are the quotient N_(P_n)(S)/(Z(P_n)S); a logically nontrivial Pauli lies in N_(P_n)(S) minus Z(P_n)S. Scalar phases and stabilizers act trivially on logical rays.
proof_obligations: Fix the sign-to-bit convention and prove the syndrome depends only on the Pauli coset modulo scalar phase.
Distinguish a stabilizer error, which is logically trivial, from a nontrivial normalizer element.

items.statement_or_definition: For a stabilizer code encoding k>0 qubits, d is the minimum weight of E in N_(P_n)(S) minus Z(P_n)S. For k=0 define d=+infinity. This is a set difference, not a product N(S)S, and excludes nontrivial scalar phases of stabilizers.
proof_obligations: Show the set is nonempty for a code with a nontrivial protected subsystem; state a convention for k=0.
items.title: QC20 Stabilizer Distance

items.statement_or_definition: A stabilizer code of distance d detects Pauli errors of weight <d and corrects unknown Pauli errors of weight at most t when 2t<d.
proof_obligations: If a Pauli anticommutes with a stabilizer, PEP=0. If it commutes and has weight below d, it belongs to Z(P_n)S and PEP is a scalar P.
For error pairs of weight ≤t, their product has weight ≤2t<d; apply the preceding dichotomy to each product and then KL. General local errors follow from expansion in the tensor-Pauli basis.

items.statement_or_definition: For C2⊆C1≤F2^n, define coset vectors |x+C2>=|C2|^(−1/2)sum_(c∈C2)|x+c>, for x in C1/C2. No extra C2-perp⊆C1 condition is needed for this nested-code convention. items.statement_or_definition: The CSS coset encoding is an isometry of k logical qubits; X^c for c∈C₂ and Z^h for h∈C₁⊥ commute and stabilize the encoded states.
proof_obligations: Prove orthogonality by disjoint cosets and normalization by |C₂|.

items.statement_or_definition: For the nested-code convention C2⊆C1 and X checks C2, Z checks C1-perp, any bounded-weight CSS recovery guaranteed by KL corrects t arbitrary qubit errors when 2t<min(d(C1),d(C2-perp)), with zero-code distances +infinity. Use syndrome decoders for C1 to correct X components and C2-perp to correct Z components; more precise distances are min wt(C1 minus C2) and min wt(C2-perp minus C1-perp).

Prove the X and Z corrections preserve code superpositions, then handle products and degeneracy using KL.

items.statement_or_definition: Input r independent commuting signed Hermitian Pauli rows excluding −I on n wires, r≤n. For pivot j=0,...,r−1: take first remaining nonidentity row, choose first nonzero unused wire and SWAP it to j. On each unused wire convert that row local X to Z with H, Y to Z with chronological S† then H, leaving Z fixed; conjugate every row with each gate. For every remaining Z at wire k≠j apply CNOT(k→j), again updating all rows, leaving the pivot as ±Z_j. If its sign is minus, apply X_j. Commuting remaining rows have no X_j; multiply each with Z_j bit 1 by the pivot to clear it. Continue on unused wires. Record gates D sending input checks to +Z_0,...,+Z_(r−1); output D† as encoder acting on |0^r> tensor logical basis |x>, together with each signed row-operation map and that logical basis convention. Invalid dependent/noncommuting/−I inputs return INVALID.
proof_obligations: Give a terminating row/column elimination algorithm with exact H/S/CNOT/SWAP updates and phase tracking.
For every branch, preserve commutation and row-space invariants; bound gate count and workspace.

items.statement_or_definition: For reference-preserving error propagation, a state is s-deviated from an encoded target when it belongs to the linear/error-channel span generated by operators supported on at most s physical coordinates of that target (include arbitrary reference tensor identity). A gadget has spread ell when each single supported fault term propagates to at most ell output coordinates per block; multi-fault supports use the union bound.

items.statement_or_definition: Conditional on a proper code correcting d located errors, block size m≥2d+1, spread ℓ, procedure bound a, and q=floor(d/(2ℓ))≥1, let A=choose(a,q+1). Under independent local CPTP faults with Aη^q<1, level-r logical failure is at most A^(−1/q)(A^(1/q)η)^((q+1)^r); N output rectangles fail with probability at most N times this bound. The rectangle recursion must partition elementary fault locations into disjoint children, 1≤q<a, and every all-good gadget must satisfy its complete reference-preserving logical action contract; overlapping extended rectangles require the separate truncation analysis. Here d is a correction capacity, not minimum code distance.
proof_obligations: Give complete finite-dimensional rectangle induction and prove the stated hypothesis 2qℓ≤d suffices at every concatenation level.
Prove that all-good top-level gadgets reproduce the ideal output law; state output total-variation error and success-probability transfer.
Choose r as the least level giving Npᵣ≤δ and derive polylogarithmic size/depth overhead with constants depending on the fixed code/gadgets.
This theorem is conditional; do not infer a universal threshold until a concrete proper universal code is proved.

items.statement_or_definition: For integer d≥2 take the square grid with vertices (i,j), 0≤i,j≤d and unit horizontal/vertical edges. Let R be the left and right vertical boundaries, including their vertices and edges. Use relative F2 chain spaces C2(all d² faces), C1(edges not in R; 2d² qubits), C0(vertices not in R). Order coordinates lexicographically. Z checks are boundaries of faces with R edges deleted; X checks are rows of the relative incidence C1→C0. Missing face/outside dual boundaries are the top and bottom; left/right are rough. Define the code by these commuting checks, without physical/topological-order premises.
proof_obligations: The relative incidence of each face boundary is zero because each nonrough vertex occurs twice; hence every X/Z check pair commutes.
Explicit check matrices, boundary identification, and chosen primal/dual strings are part of the definition. Chain/homology assertions are proved in the next theorem.

items.statement_or_definition: For this relative d×d square patch, there is one logical qubit, distance d, and each Z logical crossing has length at least d. Primal self-avoiding rough-to-rough paths of length ell are bounded by (d+1)3^ell (there are d+1 left starting edges and at most three later continuations). Dual top-to-bottom logical crossings have minimum length d+1, so both types have weight at least d.
proof_obligations: Relative vertex incidence has rank (d−1)(d+1)=d²−1: any nonrough vertex subset with zero coboundary is empty by connectivity to a rough edge. Relative face boundary has rank d²: peeling the topmost face of a nonzero 2-chain detects an undeleted horizontal edge. Thus k=2d²−(d²−1)−d²=1.

A relative cycle decomposes into closed loops and rough-to-rough paths. Same-side paths/loops bound relative face chains; a left-to-right path is the unique nontrivial class and requires d horizontal steps. A straight horizontal row attains d. Duality by the explicit check matrix gives top-to-bottom paths crossing d+1 horizontal-edge rows; no smaller nontrivial dual class exists.
Count left start heights j=0,...,d and choose at most three next edges when immediate backtracking is excluded. Logical failures can be reduced to self-avoiding paths by deleting loops.

items.title: Six-anyon braid target extends uniformly to fusion spectators
items.statement_or_definition: For n≥2 triples of τ anyons with each triple fixed to total τ and total register charge c, the code factors as (C²)^⊗n⊗V(τⁿ→c). For any adjacent triple pair, the full fixed-charge ambient space decomposes as ⊕_{a=1,τ}V(τ⁶→a)⊗V(a⊗τ^(3n−6)→c), where the second factor includes all physical spectator paths and triple multiplicities. In each local block the pair code is C⁴, with complement dimensions 1 (a=1) and 4 (a=τ). Joint density approximates T₁=U⊕(det U)⁻¹ and Tτ=U⊕diag((det U)⁻¹,1,1,1) simultaneously. The resulting global ideal extension is ⊕_a T_a⊗I; the actual braid is within δ of it on the full ambient space, so logical error and leakage are each ≤δ uniformly over spectators, including states with prior leakage.

items.title: Arbitrary-size triple-encoded braid universality
items.statement_or_definition: For every finite n, total charge c with V(τⁿ→c)≠0, unitary target U on n logical qubits, and ε>0, there is a finite normalized braid V on the triple-τ code (C²)^⊗n⊗V(τⁿ→c) such that inf_|z|=1||P_code V P_code−z U P_code||≤ε and ||(I−P_code)V P_code||≤ε, uniformly over spectator fusion states. The proof compiles exact finite QSD after replacing one-qubit U(2) factors by SU(2) representatives and storing their scalar as global-phase metadata. One-triple braid-dependent extensions agree with the lifted braid on local total charge 1 and use its target on total τ; two-triple extensions use simultaneous SU(5)×SU(8) targets. These extensions preserve the code and give whole-space error bounds, so prior leakage is covered. Phases are harmless only for uncontrolled fixed-charge computation; controlled access must track them. No efficient braid word-length or bit-time bound is claimed.
proof_obligations: Use the exact finite QSD decomposition into arbitrary one-qubit gates and CNOTs; replace each one-qubit U(2) gate by a determinant-one representative and store the scalar as a global phase. Use adjacent encoded SWAP targets to route nonadjacent logical wires; count abstract gates separately from braid letters/classical compilation.

For each one-qubit braid, decompose the global space by local triple charge 1,τ; define the ideal extension to equal the compiled lifted braid on charge 1 and the matched SU(2) target tensored with spectator identity on charge τ, proving ambient error ≤δ.

For each adjacent two-qubit target, apply the joint SU(5)×SU(8) spectator extension. Choose tolerances with sum ≤ε; code-preserving ideal extensions and unitary telescoping give projective logical error and leakage ≤ε.
